standard.title: Electrical Standards & Codes
standard.subtitle: Q&A about standards (SNI, PUIL, IEC, NEC) — never touches Revit
standard.failed: Could not reach the standards assistant
standard.clearConfirm: Clear this whole conversation? It cannot be undone.

exportImport.title: Export & Import
exportImport.note: /list_sheets shows the sheet numbers /print_pdf takes; /export writes schedules and the compliance report. Exports appear on the History page as download links once the add-in has Cloudinary credentials.

history.title: Command History
history.subtitle: The last 50 commands you sent to Revit, with their results.
history.fileNote: File links appear only when the add-in runs with `export_base_url` set. Without it, an export is recorded as a local path on the Revit PC.

admin.title: Project Access
admin.subtitle: A new account has no project access at all until it is granted here.
admin.noMembers: No members on this project yet
admin.pendingNote: These accounts have signed up but hold no project access yet. Pick a role and press Grant.
admin.searchHint: Type at least 2 letters of their name. The full list is deliberately not shown.
admin.notAdmin: You do not administer any project yet. Create one below, or ask an admin to add you to an existing one.
admin.roleNote: viewer reads only (query, export, print_pdf, list_sheets); editor may run device commands; admin may manage access.
admin.createPlaceholder: Project name, e.g. Tower B Jakarta
admin.createNote: You become admin of the project you create. System admins are given full access too, so it is visible without being asked for.

auth.haveAccount: Already have an account? Sign in
auth.checkEmail: Account created. Check your email to confirm, then sign in.
auth.accessNote: A new account has no project access yet. An admin must grant it before you can send commands to Revit.
auth.notConfigured: Supabase is not configured on this deployment. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in Vercel, then redeploy. Check /api/health to confirm.

command.confirm: This changes the model and cannot be undone from here. Continue?
command.noProject: Your account has no project access yet. Ask an admin to add you — until then no command can reach Revit.
command.roleTooLow: Your role on this project is read-only. Commands that change the model need the editor role.
command.waitingAddin: Waiting to be claimed by the add-in. If it stays here, check that Revit is open and the add-in is running.
command.roomsFailed: Could not read the room list from Revit.
command.roomsTimeout: The add-in has not answered. Check that Revit is open and the add-in is running.
command.sheetsEmpty: This model has no printable sheets.
command.setupNone: This model has no saved setups — Revit defaults will be used.
command.setupAsk: The setup list is read as soon as Revit connects.

chat.title: Ask in plain language
chat.subtitle: Say what you want. The proposed command fills the form below — you press send.
chat.placeholder: e.g. place 6 lights in Meeting 1 at 3 m
chat.checkForm: Filled into the form below. Check it, then press Send to Revit.

importExcel.title: Import Excel
importExcel.subtitle: Send a spreadsheet back into the model. An Element Id or Mark column identifies each row's element; every other column is a parameter name.
importExcel.dryRun: Dry run first — apply then roll back, to see what would change
importExcel.waiting: Waiting for Revit to process it…
importExcel.doneDry: Dry run finished — nothing in the model was changed.
importExcel.note: Same shape Export writes: export it, edit in Excel, send it back here. A column matching no parameter is reported rather than guessed at.

importTable.title: Import Table
importTable.subtitle: Bring any spreadsheet into the model as a table — column widths, row heights, and merged cells come across as they are.
importTable.targetScheduleHint: A new view, placeable on one sheet.
importTable.targetLegendHint: Reusable across many sheets. The model must already hold at least one legend — Revit does not let an add-in create the first.
importTable.viewNamePlaceholder: Leave empty to use the Excel sheet name
importTable.waiting: Waiting for Revit to draw it…
importTable.note: The result is a picture of the table, not a schedule that reads the model — Revit cannot show free-form Excel columns as a schedule. To change it, edit the spreadsheet and import again.

import.title: Import into Revit
import.subtitle: Two ways to bring a spreadsheet into the model. Pick the one that matches what is in the file.
import.whichTable: Import Table — for any spreadsheet (cost estimate, cable list, a supplier table). The table is drawn into a Revit view as it stands.
import.whichExcel: Import Excel — only for files that came from the Export button, because it needs an Element Id or Mark column to know which row belongs to which element. Used to update parameters on elements that already exist.

note.export.local_only: The file is on the PC running Revit and cannot be downloaded from here yet. Fill in the Cloudinary credentials in %APPDATA%\RevitCommandCenter\config.json so exports arrive as download links.
note.print.no_bot_token: Telegram delivery is on but the bot token is empty, so the file was not sent to any chat.
note.export_cad.no_setup: Exported with no CAD export setup, so Revit defaults were used — layers and line weights are unlikely to match the office standard.
